groups.contract: Return annotation is postponed definition metadata, not runtime type enforcement. Bind values to the exact self._stop_values object without copying, then n=len(values). For n==0 return a newly created empty list before reading direction or constructing level zero. Missing values attribute or failing length operation propagates. No mutation of detector state here.

For nonempty values, less is the result of direction == 'bullish'; native bullish chooses minimum, any other local direction chooses maximum (constructor rejects unsupported normal directions). Create a fresh outer list with level zero list(range(n)), containing positional ordinals, not candle codes or Decimal prices. The local annotation list[list[int]] does not evaluate at function execution. Set k=1. For n=1 loop never executes and returns [[0]].

While (1<<k)<=n, include exact-power-of-two final levels. prev aliases last completed level st[-1]; span=1<<(k-1), width=n-(1<<k)+1, cur=[0]*width is fresh list of width integer placeholders. For stable native list length n>0, width>=1 and number of levels is floor(log2(n))+1 including level zero; previous level width n-2^(k-1)+1. No price arithmetic.

Visit i in range(width), increasing, right excluded. Read left=prev[i], right=prev[i+span] (adjacent half-span blocks, not full-span offset); then lv=values[left], rv=values[right], in that order. Both values read even if first comparison later succeeds. Native table positions correspond to extrema of each half; values remain aliased and are not normalized again. Sequence changes or malformed data may invalidate guarantees.

Only selected directional test lv<rv for less or lv>rv otherwise is evaluated first. On truthy result write left to cur[i]; reverse directional test only if first false, write right if true. Otherwise evaluate left<=right and store left or right accordingly. No explicit price equality predicate. For stable comparable finite Decimal values, this produces earliest min/max owner by induction from level zero. Neither-strict-wins is the literal contract, not universal equality; Decimal NaN/traps or arbitrary comparator behavior can raise or differ. No rounding, conversion, tolerance, averaging or price negation.

Append fully filled cur to st by reference, then k+=1; repeat. Return the constructed mutable list of mutable levels without copying or assigning detector attributes. Native allocation, indexing, comparison and append failures propagate; no local catch or rollback. Earlier local table construction may have occurred but E15 assignment/publication happens only after successful return. E15 prior value/code assignments may remain if builder raises. No independent freshness/immutability guarantee.

Annotations are postponed metadata. Bind values to self._stop_values (not copy), read direction==bullish before computing length. Missing values or failing direction access/comparison can raise even for a nonpositive interval. Do not describe early return as occurring before all attribute access.

Compute length=right-left+1 inclusive, then if length<=0 return original left immediately. No sparse-table access, price access, bounds clamp or validation of left on this branch. Nonpositive length is not necessarily a valid position; return may be out of range. Arithmetic/type/comparison failures before the guard propagate.

For positive integer length choose k=length.bit_length()-1=floor(log2(length)); then read self._extreme_sparse into st, i1=st[k][left], i2=st[k][right-(1<<k)+1] in that order. Each block length 2^k, inclusive left-aligned and right-aligned, together cover requested interval for valid bounds; overlap or coincide (exact power of two including length one), never leave gap. Two reads even when blocks coincide. No local coercion, endpoint check, clamp, fallback or repair. Negative list indices wrap if in range, out-of-range levels or indices raise if reached; malformed stored positions may wrap, error or produce incorrect owner. Positive non-integer length lacking bit_length raises; arbitrary custom types may dispatch differently.

Read lv=values[i1] then rv=values[i2] before any price comparison. Both accesses use cached positions unchanged, not candle codes. Native negative position may index from end; invalid position raises; no check that values belong to intended interval, same length or current geometry. No normalization.

Test first directional strict superiority (lv<rv for bullish, lv>rv otherwise), return i1 immediately if true. Only if first false test reverse strict superiority and return i2 if true. Otherwise return i1 if i1<=i2 else i2. No explicit equality test, no price arithmetic. On stable valid ordinary comparable Decimal data, earliest directional extreme among two covering blocks is earliest extreme of inclusive query; length one returns sole position subject to access/comparison validity. NaN, malformed comparators or stale/mutated table are conditional exceptions to that inference. No mutation of native cached data, no catch, retry, rollback or local recovery.
